action: Ask the bank that holds the account to confirm it is recorded under your foreign passport (a 境外个人 account). The bank sets this from the ID used when the account was opened.

Collect the documents that show where the RMB came from and how much: for salary, the employment contract and payslips; for other income, the contract or payment record. The rule calls these 有交易额的购汇资金来源材料.

Get tax evidence for that income from the Chinese tax office: a tax payment certificate (完税证明), a tax-exemption certificate, or the tax filing form. Bank-deposit interest earned since 9 October 2008 is exempt.

For a single payment above USD 50,000 in a listed category (work pay, dividends, property-sale income and others) the tax filing rule (对外支付税务备案) comes into play; ask the tax office which form of tax evidence it will issue. The filing is a record, not a tax.
If tax on the income was never withheld, pay it. The law makes the taxpayer liable when the payer did not withhold.
Take passport, source documents and tax evidence to the bank and buy USD. The bank applies its selling rate at that moment.
Wire the USD to your own account in the United States. Bank of China's published personal fee is 0.1% (RMB 50-260) plus RMB 150 cable.
Keep every document. On the U.S. side: FBAR if your foreign accounts exceeded USD 10,000 at any time in the year, Form 8938 above its thresholds, and report any currency gain.
Find the bank's original exchange slip (兑换水单) from when you converted foreign currency into RMB. It must be dated within the last 24 months.
Take your passport and the slip to the bank. You can change back up to the unused RMB from that conversion.
The bank sells you USD at its selling rate.
Wire the USD to your own U.S. account, or keep it in a foreign-currency account and wire later (see L03).
Without a slip, only USD 500 equivalent a day can be changed back on the passport alone.
Check with the bank how much of the balance is held as foreign currency in a foreign-currency account in your name.
With your passport, instruct the bank to remit it abroad. For a foreign individual, remittance from the FX account is done on valid ID; unused FX that was wired in can go back the way it came.
Pay the wire fee: 0.1% (RMB 50-260) plus RMB 150 cable at Bank of China's published personal rate.
U.S. side: the account still counts for FBAR and Form 8938 for the year.
Complete the sale and the title transfer at the housing authority. The remittance can only be done after the transfer of ownership is registered.
Pay the taxes of the sale and obtain the tax certificate. Income tax on a property transfer is 20% of the gain (price minus original cost and reasonable expenses).
Take to the bank: passport; the transfer contract registered with the housing authority and the registration proof; the tax certificate (above USD 50,000 this is normally the tax filing form).
Ask for no more than the sale price minus the taxes of that sale (your share if co-owned). The bank checks the amount against the tax certificate.
The bank converts and wires the USD to your account abroad.
Obtain proof of your right to inherit (for example a notarised inheritance certificate) and the property documents of the person who died.
Turn the inherited assets into RMB and get a tax certificate from the tax office where the estate's property is located.
Get a certificate of your residence abroad issued or certified by a Chinese embassy or consulate.

Apply once, for the whole estate, to the SAFE office of the place where the decedent's household registration was: written application, application form, ID, inheritance proof, property and tax documents.

After SAFE issues the approval (核准件), take it to the bank. The bank buys USD and remits it directly to your own account in your country of residence, in one or several transfers. Cash withdrawal is not allowed.
U.S. side: if the bequest from the foreign estate is more than USD 100,000 in the year, file Form 3520 by the due date. The form reports the receipt; a late filing can cost 5% a month, up to 25%.
Confirm you fit the definition: a person who moved from mainland China to another country, moving property owned in China before obtaining emigrant status.

Gather: proof from the public security bureau that your Chinese hukou was cancelled; a settlement certificate issued or certified by a Chinese embassy or consulate; property documents; tax certificates from where the property or income arose.
Apply once, for everything you intend to move, to the SAFE office of your former hukou location (written application, the applicant form and the application form).
After approval, the bank may remit the approved amount in one transfer or in instalments. The 2004 staging rule (half, then half a year later) was removed in 2014.
The bank remits directly to your own account in your country of residence.
Confirm you hold the PRC Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card. A work or residence permit is not the same document.
With that card, buy up to USD 50,000 equivalent per calendar year at the bank or in its app. No source documents are needed inside the yearly amount.
Wire the USD to your own account abroad.
For anything above the yearly amount, use the documented-income route (L01). Do not use other people's amounts (P01).
Ask your bank whether it handles personal cross-border RMB remittance for current-account income. The PBOC's 2018 notice supports it; individual banks decide whether to offer it.
Prepare the same income and tax evidence as for L01. The bank's exact document list was not verified in this pass.
Remit the RMB to an account in your own name outside the mainland that can receive RMB.
Convert the RMB to USD at that bank. Its rate and fees are not officially published, so the cost is left blank on this site.
Confirm the company has distributable profit and has paid its taxes.
Pass a board or shareholder profit-distribution resolution.
The company withholds 20% individual income tax on the dividend.
For a remittance above USD 50,000, complete the tax filing and give the bank the original filing form with the resolution.
The bank converts and remits the after-tax dividend to you.
U.S. side: the dividend is taxable income; Chinese tax paid may be claimed as a foreign tax credit on Form 1116.
Make sure the RMB account has a UnionPay debit card that works abroad.
Withdraw cash at ATMs outside the mainland: at most RMB 10,000 per card per day, and RMB 100,000 per person per calendar year counting all your cards.
Bank of China charges RMB 12 plus 1% of each withdrawal, at most RMB 112. The network exchange rate and any fee from the ATM owner are extra and not published in one place.
Stop at the yearly cap: going over it suspends overseas withdrawals for the rest of that year and the next. Using someone else's card is prohibited (P06).
Bringing more than USD 10,000 in cash into the U.S. must be declared on FinCEN Form 105.
Buy the foreign currency lawfully first (L01, L02 or L07). Carrying cash does not replace the document rules.
Up to USD 5,000 per trip: customs lets it through. USD 5,000-10,000: ask the bank for a carrying permit (《携带外汇出境许可证》) when you withdraw the cash.
Do not carry more than USD 10,000: a SAFE permit is needed and is in principle not granted.
On arrival in the U.S., declare if you (or your family or group together) carry more than USD 10,000.
